17 A horizontal cylinder of cross-sectional area A is fitted with a frictionless piston and contains air at
pressure P. It is immersed in hot water and the length of the air column increases from x to y. The
pressure P is constant.

Which equation represents the work done by the trapped air during this process?
A
PAy
B
–PAy
C
PA(y – x)
D
–PA(y – x)

hints: Notice the air column length changes from $x$ to $y$ with cross-sectional area $A$, so find the increase in volume $A(y - x)$ rather than using $y$ alone.
Recall that at constant pressure $P$, the work done by a gas equals $P$ multiplied by the change in volume.
Check the sign: the trapped air expands and pushes the frictionless piston outward, so work done by the air must be positive.
walkthrough: Identify the change: initial volume is $Ax$ and final volume is $Ay$, so the increase in volume is $Ay - Ax = A(y - x)$.
Recall the rule for constant pressure: work done by the gas is $W = P \Delta V$.
An equivalent view is force on piston $F = PA$ moved through distance $(y - x)$, so $W = F \times$ distance $= PA(y - x)$.
Check the sign: expansion means the gas does work on the piston, so $W$ is positive, not negative.
This matches $PA(y - x)$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This uses only the final volume $Ay$ instead of the change in volume. Work depends on the increase $y - x$, not on $y$ alone.

B.explanation: This uses only the final volume $Ay$ and has a negative sign. The gas expands, so work done by the gas is positive.

C.explanation: The volume increase is $A(y - x)$, so at constant pressure the work done by the gas is $P$ times volume change, $PA(y - x)$.

D.explanation: The magnitude $PA(y - x)$ is correct for $P$ times volume change, but the sign is wrong because work done by an expanding gas is positive.
